About Event

​All Agents, Now in Sync.

​Join us for the BAND Dark Factory Buildathon, powered by HackerSquad, at AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco on Friday, November 13, 2026, from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM PST.

​Spend the day building an AI Software Factory, where AI coding agents work together to produce working software from specifications using BAND Desktop.

​About Band

​BAND provides infrastructure for collaboration between AI agents and humans. Its shared interaction layer lets agents communicate, delegate, and coordinate while keeping their own tools, models, and memory. BAND also offers tools for developers to coordinate coding agents in a shared workspace.

​What to expect

​Gain deeper understanding of how AI coding agents work together and what it takes to make an efficient and successful AI Software Factory. Come on your own or with a team. Developers, designers, founders, and curious builders of all experience levels are welcome.

​Bring your laptop, charger, and the tools or accounts you need for your project. Explore the BAND website, documentation and hacker guide before the event. The final agenda will be shared closer to the event.

Berkeley x DeepMind Hackathon: Build. Ship. Pitch. Win.
Win up to $5M in Seed Funding | November 14th, 10:00 AM–6:00 PM PT*
In partnership with “Haas AI Club” and "Girls into VC" @ UC Berkeley
Join us for an elite hackathon where you'll build cutting-edge projects with Google Gemini and earn 30-minute pitch meetings with top-tier VCs.
🏆 The Prize
Top teams will be judged by representatives from Google, Berkeley, Stanford, and multiple venture capital funds.
Grand Prize — VC Pitch Access: A 30-minute private pitch meeting with selected funds from our judging panel — VCs writing 500K–5M seed checks. Pitch your hackathon project or your existing startup.
Google AI Studio Track (sponsored by DeepMind):
In-Person: share of $15K in GCP credits
Online: share of $5K in GCP credits
*Investment not guaranteed. The prize is pitch access only — winning teams gain meeting access but must earn investment through their pitch and business fundamentals.
📅 Event Schedule
10:00 AM — Registration & Breakfast: light refreshments and networking with fellow builders
10:30 AM — Opening Ceremony & Rules Briefing: official rules and competition format
11:30 AM — Hacking Begins: 3-hour build sprint
2:30 PM — Submission Deadline (hard stop): all submissions must be in
2:30 PM — Late Lunch: sandwiches, beverages, and networking
3:30 PM — Semi-Finalists Announced: top teams selected for live pitches
4:00 PM — Live Finals: top teams pitch on stage (5-min pitch + 5-min Q&A)
5:30 PM — Winners Announced
6:00 PM — Event Wrap-Up
⚖️ Meet the Judges
Google & Google DeepMind
 Amit Vadi — Head of Community, Google DeepMind
 Joana Carrasqueira — Senior Manager, Google DeepMind
 Naman Goyal — Researcher, Google DeepMind
Venture Capital

 Iris Sun — Partner, 500 Global
 Ashtan Jordan — Principal, Precursor Ventures
 Utkarsh Bajpai — Investor, General Catalyst
 Tanya Jomaa — Investor, Redpoint Ventures
 Tracy Liu — Investor, M12 (Microsoft's Venture Fund)
 Tessa Osborne — Investor, Plug and Play
Berkeley & Stanford
 Ben Fong — Berkeley SkyDeck
 Devansh Shah — Haas AI Club @ Berkeley
 Emile Shah — President, Girls into VC @ Berkeley
 Prof. Nikesh Kotecha — Head of Data Science, Stanford Health Care
🌐 Online Track
Can't make it to campus? We've added an Online Track for remote participants:
No live streaming or video conferencing — work on your own schedule
Submission deadline: end of day, November 14
Same deliverables as in-person participants
Judging based on traction — same conditions as Phase 2 (7-day social engagement tracking)
Prize pool: $5K in GCP credits
VC pitch access for top submissions
Build with Gemini, ship a prototype, post your demo, and let your network do the talking. Top submissions get 30-minute meetings with funds.
📋 Submission Requirements
All projects must use the Google Gemini model. Each team must submit the following by 2:30 PM sharp:
One-Pager for the team — Short plain text describing your team and your pedigree
One-Pager for the idea — Short plain text describing your idea and prototype
Hosted Prototype — Working demo link (via Google AI Studio & Google Cloud Run)
2-Minute Video — Team introduction and elevator pitch
1-Minute Video — Prototype demo (Playcast)
Code Repository — Link via Google AI Studio sharing
Data Usage & Judging Consent: By submitting your prototype Playcast, you authorize organizers to use your submission in paid social ads (e.g., Facebook). Real-world performance metrics (CPM, CTR, CPC, etc.) will be collected and used as core market validation data for Phase 2 (post-event) judging. You may opt out by notifying organizers prior to submission; data sharing with sponsors and investors is a condition of participation.
⚖️ Judging Criteria
Technical Feasibility — Does it actually work?
Innovation & Novelty — Is the approach creative or clever?
Real-World Applicability — Would people genuinely use it?
Market Potential & Fundability — Could this become venture-backable?
Go-to-Market Traction — Social engagement on your demo video (likes, shares, views)
Social Engagement Component: Your demo YouTube video must be shared publicly. Engagement counts toward your score:
Phase 1 — Tracked during the hackathon (5:00 PM cutoff)
Phase 2 — Continued tracking for 2 weeks post-event (viral reach + Playcast metrics)
🎯 Competition Format
Semi-Finals: All submissions undergo asynchronous review by the judging panel.
Finals: Top teams advance to live presentations — 10 minutes per team (5-min pitch + 5-min Q&A) on stage before the full panel of VCs and special guests. Winners announced at 5:30 PM.
Whether you're a solo developer, have a team, or are already building a startup (some invited participants are at Series A stage), this event is a unique opportunity to showcase your work to decision-makers at leading venture funds.
❓ FAQ
Can I pitch an existing startup? Absolutely! If you win, you can pitch either your hackathon project or your existing company during the 30-minute VC meetings.
What's the team size limit? Up to 5 people.
Can I participate solo? Yes.
Can I participate remotely? Yes! The Online Track has the same deliverables, with submissions due by end of day, November 14. No live streaming — judging is based on 7-day social engagement (Phase 2 conditions). The Online Track has a $5K GCP credits prize pool.
When do VC meetings happen? Winners will schedule 30-minute pitch meetings with selected funds after the event.
What should I bring? Laptop, charger, and your best ideas!
📌 Age Requirement
This event is open to participants 18 years and older. Valid ID may be required for check-in.

AIE Code Summit 2026 Hackathon
San Francisco, CASat, Nov 7 at 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (PST)

Welcome to the AI Engineer Code Summit Hackathon!

We've teamed up with Meta, Google Deepmind, MongoDB, Subquadratic, and Fetch.ai to host a one day hackathon for working on frontier AI engineering problems, the weekend before the official summit.

Coding agents can already write code, but what happens when they must understand, finish, and judge real software on their own? Come build agents that close the gap, building systems that get measurably better with every run, reconstruct software from imperfect evidence, and verify what other agents ship before it merges.

Speakers and judges will be drawn from the top of the industry, including Ivan Leo from Google DeepMind and Mike Beltzner from Meta.

Win $11,000 in total prizes, including $5,000 for the best use of the Meta Model API!

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Space is limited. Maximum team size is four. All attendees must submit an application and be approved to attend.

About Event
​NASA International Space Apps Challenge – Mountain View 2026

​The world’s largest space and science hackathon returns to Mountain View in partnership with the NASA Ames Research Center. Join a global community of innovators tackling real-world challenges under this year’s theme: "The Next Frontier."

​Details

​Event Dates: November 14–15, 2026

​Registration Opens: August 25, 2026

​Format: Online (open to global participants with live streams, networking sessions, and collaborative support)

​Register Here: spaceappschallenge.org/2026/local-events/mountain-view/

​Who Can Participate?

​You don't need a coding background to make an impact. We welcome multidisciplinary thinkers of all backgrounds:

​Coders, engineers, and data scientists

​Designers, artists, and storytellers

​Educators, writers, and domain specialists

​Space enthusiasts ready to solve bold problems

​Why Join?

​Work with NASA Open Data: Build solutions, tools, and creative projects using real space agency datasets.

​Global Scale & Collaboration: Organized under the NASA Science Mission Directorate alongside 11+ international space agencies.

​Skill Building & Networking: Connect directly with a worldwide network of technologists, scientists, and creatives.

​Reserve your spot on the official event page and get ready to build the next frontier.

​Official Sponsor Spotlight: Microsoft Academy! 🌌

​We are thrilled to welcome Microsoft Academy as an Official Sponsor for NASA Space Apps Mountain View!

​As innovators, coders, scientists, and storytellers gather in Mountain View to tackle real-world challenges on Earth and in space using NASA’s open data, Microsoft is equipping our hackers with the cloud compute, AI tools, and NASA-inspired training modules needed to take your projects to orbit.

​Whether you're building machine learning models to analyze satellite imagery, predicting rocket launch conditions, or deploying a full-stack space app, check out these free Microsoft Learning Resources & Tools to power up your hackathon weekend:

​📚 NASA-Inspired Microsoft Learn Modules & Paths:

​Analyze Space Rocks with Python & AI: Microsoft Learn – Analyze Rock Images with AI

​Day of Data – Rockets (NASA STEM Partnership): Microsoft Learn – Day of Data: Rockets

​Introduction to the Data Science Process: Microsoft Learn – Data Science Process

​Plan a Rocket Launch with Python & VS Code: Microsoft Learn – Learn with Dr. G

​🛠️ Cloud, AI & Earth Observation Platforms for Hackers:

​Microsoft Learn Hub (All Training Paths): learn.microsoft.com

​Microsoft Planetary Computer (Earth Observation Data & APIs): planetarycomputer.microsoft.com

​Azure for Students ($100 Free Cloud Credit – No Credit Card Required): azure.microsoft.com/free/students

​A huge thank you to Microsoft Academy for empowering the Mountain View space-tech community! Let’s build something out of this world. 🌍✨
